profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Superhuman
profile.summary: I am a software developer based out of Seattle. I am currently working at Patreon, where I'm leading the development of our identity verification systems.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer/Tech Lead
positions.description:
I serve as the technical lead of Patreon's Risk team where I am currently leading the development of a new User Identity platform that will streamline the collection and storage of sensitive user data. This platform will serve multiple client use cases such as know your customer checks, tax form generation, and age verification.

Some of my other projects include:
- Designing and implementing Patreon's know your customer program
- Leveraging AI tools to quickly improve the usability of internal Fraud and compliance tooling
- Implementing a system to automate the capture and validation of customer identification data

positions.title: Software Engineer 3
positions.description:
- Designed and implemented an age verification system to verify the identities of hundreds of thousands of 18+ content creators
- Implemented an event stream to hundreds of transaction events per second the Unit21 transaction monitoring system
- Created a tax data collection to quickly comply with a short notice EU tax regulation

positions.title: Supplemental Instructor
positions.description: I work in the Computer Science department as a supplemental instructor for the introductory CS course. As an SI instructor, I create exercises and lessons plans that help the students deepen their understanding of programming concepts, I lead collaborative sessions where students learn in an interactive and hands-on environment, and I help the students understand Python programming. This job has helped me gain a deeper understanding of the fundamental concepts of programming, and it has helped me grow my abilities as a leader.

positions.title: Cluster Manager
positions.description: I currently work as a cluster manager for the St. Olaf Computer Science department. As a cluster manager, I help to manage and maintain St. Olaf's parallel computing resources. This job has exposed me to a wide variety of tasks such as documentation, web development, tech support, etc. Because of this, I've become very good at adapting to novel challenges and learning new skills on the fly.

positions.title: Summer Researcher
positions.description: I worked as a summer researcher in the Computer Science department of St. Olaf. My primary focus for the summer was to help develop TSGL, a graphics library designed for multicore machines. Due to my previous experience working as a cluster manager, I also took on a support role for the other student researcher's projects. This position helped me develop my C++/OpenGL programming skills and taught me how to be a reliable and helpful team member.

positions.title: Tech-Support Intern
positions.description: I worked as a summer intern for the User Support department at the Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center. My role at the hospital was to help install hardware and software in preparation for the hospital's transition to a new payment system. During my time in this position, I worked with numerous hospital workers who were unhappy about the changes at the hospital. For this reason, I became comfortable at working in high-pressure environments and diplomatically navigating problematic interactions.
